title: Bug: [yang] sonic-kdump.yang ssh_string accepts POSIX-invalid usernames
author: xq9mend
body:
### Is it platform specific

generic

### Importance or Severity

Critical

### Description of the bug

**Description**

The `ssh_string` leaf in `sonic-kdump.yang` uses:

    pattern "([a-zA-Z0-9._%+-]+@([a-zA-Z0-9.-]+|[0-9]{1,3}(\\.[0-9]{1,3}){3}))";

The user portion `[a-zA-Z0-9._%+-]+` allows the first character to be
any of `. _ % + -`, but POSIX login names (per `useradd(8)` /
NAME_REGEX) must start with `[a-zA-Z_]`. Values like `-x@host`,
`.x@host`, `+x@host` pass YANG validation but cannot correspond to a
real account on the remote kdump target — the SSH login will always
fail.

A leading `-` also makes the value look like a CLI option flag when
passed positionally to downstream tools.

**Steps to reproduce**

    config kdump ssh-string -- '-foo@10.0.0.1'   # accepted by YANG

**Expected**

Pattern restricts first char of the user part to `[a-zA-Z_]`:

    pattern "([a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9._%+-]*@([a-zA-Z0-9.-]+|[0-9]{1,3}(\\.[0-9]{1,3}){3}))";

**Affected file**

`src/sonic-yang-models/yang-models/sonic-kdump.yang:65`

comments.body:
I’ve submitted a PR to address this issue: #26663 

The fix updates the ssh_string YANG pattern to enforce POSIX-compliant usernames,
preventing invalid configurations that would fail at runtime.

Please review and let me know if any changes are needed.

linkedPullRequests.title: [yang] Restrict ssh_string username to POSIX-compliant format
linkedPullRequests.author: KeshavSM10
linkedPullRequests.body:
Fixes #26641 

1] Problem
The existing ssh_string YANG pattern allows usernames starting with characters
such as '-', '.', '+', or digits. These are not valid POSIX login names.

As a result:
- The configuration is accepted at the YANG validation layer.
- SSH attempts fail at runtime because the username is invalid.
- This leads to silent failures in remote kdump dump transfer.

2] Root Cause
The regex:
[a-zA-Z0-9._%+-]+

allows any of these characters at the start of the username, without enforcing
POSIX-compliant username rules.

3] Solution
Update the pattern to enforce a valid starting character:

[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9._%+-]*

This ensures:
- The username starts with a letter or underscore.
- Remaining characters follow the existing allowed set.
- Host validation logic remains unchanged.

4] Impact
- Invalid usernames are rejected at configuration time.
- Prevents runtime SSH failures.
- Improves system reliability and debugging correctness for kdump.

5] Validation
Tested via logical validation of regex behavior:

Rejected inputs:
- '-foo@10.0.0.1'
- '.user@host'
- '+abc@host'
- '1user@host'

Accepted inputs:
- 'user@10.0.0.1'
- 'abc_123@host'
- 'a@host'

6] Scope
- Change is limited to YANG schema validation.
- No impact on runtime logic or other modules.
